validity.recommendation: Keep the row. Verify the actual in-service (commissioning) date before locking Status=operating: independent evidence shows it was still in hydrotest/drying in May 2025 and only demonstrably carrying gas by April 2026. Consider correcting LengthKnown 8 -> 7.5 km, and treat EndLocation 'North Rumaila' as the gas's processing DESTINATION, not the physical terminus of this ~8 km pipe.
validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE: real and confirmed by >=2 independent sources. The GEM row rests on a single citation (alsharqpaper, all 8 wiki backlinks trace to it), which is thin, but independent corroboration exists: (1) Al-Sharq newspaper (alsharqpaper) reports the Oil Projects Company (SCOP) implementing a project 'to support natural gas production in the Majnoon oil field'; (2) SCOP's own bulletin (Facebook/Oil2017, verified) gives length 8 km; (3) Al-Harir news agency (Apr 2026) describes the operational 'Majnoon field gas transmission line' being used to route Ben Omar-field gas to the North Rumaila NGL/liquefaction plant. Three separate origins -> exists, high confidence.

CLASSIFICATION: correct as gas transmission. Arabic sources call it 'الخط الناقل لغاز حقل مجنون' (the Majnoon-field gas TRANSMISSION line); it carries associated gas from the Majnoon field liquid trap to NGL processing and feeds the strategic line supplying power stations. Fuel=Gas, PipelineType=transmission both hold. NOT an oil/NGL line and NOT in the GulfPub Iraq oil roster -> no cross-commodity misclassification.

DUPLICATE: none. No other roster row is a Majnoon->North Rumaila ~8 km / 24 in gas line; distinct from P2234 (North Rumela-Khor Al-Zubair, 87 km/42 in) and the other Basra-area rows. NOTE: do NOT conflate with the separate Basra Gas Company tie-in that laid a 5 km / 20 in flexible pipe to bring Ben Omar-field gas onto the Majnoon line (alharirnews) — that is a different project with different specs; P6826 is the 8 km / 24 in Majnoon line itself.

STATUS CAVEAT (main issue): the live sheet shows Status=operating, StartYear1=2025 (updated 2025-07-16). gem.wiki still shows 'Construction'. The sheet's own Status [ref] (alsharqpaper) does NOT contain 'operating' — its title translates to SCOP *beginning to implement* the project (construction commencement, retrieved 2024-08). SCOP's May 2025 completion bulletin states the line was then 'completing hydrostatic testing and drying' — i.e. mechanically complete but still in commissioning, NOT yet operating. By April 2026 (alharirnews) the line is demonstrably in service (Ben Omar gas routed through it to North Rumaila). So 'operating' is defensible as of 2026 but was premature when set in mid-2025, and gem.wiki is simply stale. Not a silent pass: flagged for a commissioning-date check.

ATTRIBUTION: Owner/Operator = Oil Projects Company 'SCOP' (confirmed, matches wiki). FuelSource = Majnoon Oil Field (confirmed associated gas). StartState=Basrah correct. EndPrefecture='North Rumaila' is the NGL processing DESTINATION (Ar Ratawi / North Rumaila BGC plant, ~75 km W of Basra), not the physical end of an 8 km pipe — see route caveat.

SPEC: Diameter 24 in CONFIRMED by two sources (alsharqpaper + SCOP bulletin). Length: sheet 8 km; SCOP's precise figure is 7,500 m (7.5 km) — round-up, minor. Capacity blank and left blank (the 600 t/day LPG and 70-80 MMcf/d figures in the sources belong to the downstream Ben Omar/BGC NGL output, not this pipe's throughput — not forced).

fills.researcher_notes: FuelSource [ref] was blank (MISSING_REF). Both sources identify the line as carrying associated gas from the Majnoon oil field ('حقل مجنون'). Two independent origins -> high.

Capacity left blank deliberately. Sources give downstream NGL output figures (500-600 t/day LPG; 70-80 MMcf/d of Ben Omar gas) tied to the North Rumaila plant and the separate Ben Omar tie-in, not a throughput for this 8 km / 24 in line. No defensible pipe-capacity number -> not forced.

routes.start_name: Majnoon oil field liquid trap / gas-gathering facility, Basrah governorate, Iraq
routes.end_name: Tie-in into the Majnoon-field gas transmission system (~8 km from the Majnoon liquid trap); gas ultimately processed at the North Rumaila / Ar Ratawi NGL plant (Basrah Gas Company), ~75 km W of Basra
routes.corridor_desc: The physical pipe is short (SCOP: 7,500 m; sheet 8 km), 24 in, so it CANNOT span Majnoon field to the North Rumaila NGL plant (~75-90 km SW). The sourced corridor is therefore local: it runs from the Majnoon field liquid trap/gas facility (NE of Basra, ~31.30N 47.36E, near the Maysan border) a few km to a tie-in with the existing Majnoon->North Rumaila gas transmission line. 'North Rumaila' in the sheet is the gas's downstream PROCESSING destination (Ar Ratawi NGL plant, ~75 km W of Basra), not this pipe's physical terminus. Start point is well-anchored to a named field; the ~8 km physical end (a tie-in point) could not be geolocated, so its coordinates are left null. Corridor bounded to the Majnoon field area within Basrah governorate.
routes.researcher_notes: Start coordinates anchored to the Majnoon oil field (latitude.to / Wikipedia: ~31.30N, 47.36E; ~60 km from Basra near the Maysan/Iran border) — the liquid trap is a facility within that field, so this is a defensible field-level point, not an invented one. End coordinates deliberately left null: the ~8 km physical terminus is an unnamed tie-in point I could not geolocate, and the North Rumaila / Ar Ratawi NGL plant (the stated downstream destination) is ~75 km away and cannot be this short pipe's endpoint. No coordinates fabricated. Route accuracy suggested 'low' — corridor bounded to the Majnoon field area but exact alignment unknown; this is a suggestion only, not for auto-application.

summary: P6826 Majnoon Gas Pipeline is real, correctly classed as a SCOP gas transmission line (Majnoon assoc. gas -> North Rumaila NGL), not a duplicate; diameter 24 in confirmed, length ~7.5 km (sheet 8), but Status=operating was premature (commissioning in May 2025; in service by Apr 2026) and 'North Rumaila' is the gas destination, not this 8 km pipe's physical end.
